title: Relation
description: A typed, dated link between two actors — the thing edges cannot say, because an edge runs between events. The id is derived, from--to--type, so the same relation cannot be filed twice (rule 2). Six types, closed: a missing one is reported in STATUS.md, never replaced by a generic one. Which kind of actor may stand at each end is rule 19.

sources.description: A relation is an assertion about two actors, so it cites at least one source, as an edge does (rule 6).

type.description: regime-of: `from` is a regime of the state `to` (Estado Novo → Portugal). succeeded: `from` was succeeded by `to` (British India → Republic of India). member-of: a person belongs to a party or body. part-of: a body belongs to the state or body it was part of. led: a person headed `to`. allied-with: symmetric, and the only one that is.

when.description: How long the relation held. end: null means it still does. A succession is an instant: start and end are the same year.

note.description: Optional, short, and written by a person: what a bare type and two dates cannot say. Carried in the topology, so an actor's card draws its relations without fetching one record each.
